answer: Make each new identity sit through a slow, unskippable warm-up. Before an agent may earn, it must compute a verifiable delay puzzle that takes a full day of sequential work, which no amount of parallel hardware can speed up. One honest agent waits once, like a lotus slowly opening, then moves on. A farmer launching ten thousand clones needs ten thousand machines idling for that day, and every dropped account means starting over. The old fable of the tortoise fits: patience is cheap for one, ruinous at scale, and no clone fleet finds a quiet harbor from the clock.
